text: If you're wondering whether that was just me, the research on DMSO and the heart has only been in animals and lab dishes so far, but it points that way. Rats given it for three days before a heart attack lost about three quarters less heart muscle (nobody gave it to them after the attack started, though). And since most heart attacks come from a clot blocking an artery, it's good that DMSO also slowed clotting, in mice and in human platelets (the blood cells that start clots) in a dish.
reader: a friend whose companion on a drug has chest pain, deciding whether DMSO with magnesium chloride on the chest is worth using before the next paragraph tells them when to call medics

Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")?
